svg.aria-label: Plan view of the fuel system after the swap, route A, seen from above with the front of the car to the left; schematic, not to scale. Under the rear seat, your Touring's tank stays and takes the donor's in-tank set: delivery unit 16142229684 (pump and right sender) in the right half with baffle 16112229656 under it, and the left sender 16142229683 and jet pump 16142282208 in the left half; the return flow drives the jet pump, whose transfer pipe goes into the baffle. The M3 pipe set 16112283288 is pushed onto the pump and ends in a quick-connector for the M3 rear feed; its return hose is clamped to the tank's return nipple. The lines run along the left floor to the filter-regulator under the left front floor: a new M3 filter on the donor's regulator housing and 5-bar regulator. The feed path is all quick-connectors, from the pipe set to the rear feed, the filter and the housing to the front feed; the return is hose and clamps. The housing carries TP1, the threaded test fitting. The front feed goes to the S54 feed pipe, probably through a quick-connector, and on to the rail, which has no test port. The vacuum hose, in its metal sleeve, runs from the regulator to the S54's idle-air pipe, and the M3 front purge line from your rear purge line to the S54 purge valve, whose hose ends in a quick-connector. Your filler pot, filler pipe, vent pipe, liquid-vapour separator 16136752641, canister and leak-test pump 16137193479 stay; at the filler only the flap changes, to the M3's 51172695524. The separator sits in the right rear wheel well, inside the arch-graft zone, and comes out for the arch work. With the spare well kept the canister stays fore and aft. With an M3 floor, expect the M3 holder 16132229735, crosswise; the Phase 5 mock-up decides: under 25 mm to the muffler or its right hanger, the M3 holder; 25 mm or more, either position works. Either way the canister and leak-test pump must keep working. Relay K96 stays behind the glovebox. Test hookups for Phase 7, engine out, with at least 10 L in the tank: a gauge on TP1 for T1 and T2; the return line off at the housing into a graduated container of 2 L or more for T3; a switch with a 15 A inline fuse across K96's socket pins 6 and 2 to run the pump; a meter from the pump connector to the battery posts for T4; and TP2, a gauge on the front feed's capped end before the engine is in.
